A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PO-MHP research work. Their main text, appendices A–Q, equations, proofs, figures, and tables are available and matchable despite reformatting.

before.justification: Section 6 and Appendix Q report original synthetic causal-recovery experiments, runtime measurements, and cellular-network results.

after.justification: The original empirical results remain, supplemented by low-sample and asymmetric-path experiments in Appendix Q.3.

M1.justification: The shared-kernel Hawkes model, observed-surrogate construction, rank tests, and two-phase discovery procedure in Algorithms 1–3 are retained. Changes to simulation parameters and graph matching concern evaluation.

E1.justification: Appendix Q.3 adds synthetic scenarios with unequal latent-path lengths, violating the symmetric-path assumption. The original synthetic graph families, larger graph, and cellular-network tasks remain. The added 5k-sample experiment changes sample size rather than task coverage.

E2.justification: Retained comparisons use the same six baselines. The new 5k-sample Case 1 comparison in Table 4 includes SHP, NPHC, THP, RLCD, and LPCMCI but explicitly excludes Hier. Rank, which participates in the retained Case 1 comparison in Figure 4.

E3.justification: Q.1 changes synthetic coefficients from [0.80,0.99], with [0.40,0.80] for Case 1, to [0.90,0.99] for latent-involving edges and [0.30,0.50] for other edges. Q.2 adds division and merging to latent-node matching against ground truth. These substantially revise reported generation and scoring protocols; the PDFs do not establish whether retained experiments were rerun. Table 4 also introduces a 5k-sample evaluation.

E4.justification: Q.3 adds two focused robustness analyses: reduced sample availability and violations created by inserting one or two intermediate latents along one path. Existing discretization, rank-threshold, rank-faithfulness, scalability, and merged-device analyses remain.

E5.justification: v2 reports averages without explicit empirical standard deviations. v3 Tables 4–5 introduce mean-and-standard-deviation reporting; Table 4 specifies ten runs. Existing ten-run reporting remains, without an asserted increase in runs.

E6.justification: Existing figure results and corresponding tables retain their values, including cellular-network F1=0.76. New Table 4 reports 5k-sample F1=0.71 for Ours (Hawkes) versus 0.96 for SHP, alongside 0.74 for Ours (Discrete). Table 5 adds asymmetric-path F1-scores of 0.92 and 0.89. These are additional results, not same-setting improvements over v2.

T1.justification: Proposition 4.5 and Theorems 4.7–4.8 explicitly require nonempty remaining subprocess sets. Appendix K revises Eq. 12 using pathwise coefficient products and integral sums, adding an exponential-kernel derivation and reasoning about leading zeros. These are localized formal revisions; the other principal results and proofs remain.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and concluding contribution claims retain the same scope: discrete-time representation, conditional identifiability, and two-phase discovery without prior knowledge of latent subprocesses.

C2.justification: v3 interprets the new tests as evidence of practical robustness with limited data and unequal latent-path lengths, offering an exponential-kernel explanation for the latter. The conclusion specifically identifies node-specific decay rates and lower computational complexity as future targets. Existing heterogeneous-device and missing-edge qualifications remain in Q.4.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 adds practical guidance to select the bin width through grid search over structurally stable values. Q.1–Q.2 revise documented simulation parameters and graph-matching rules. The simulation library, lag counts, hardware information, and dataset-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds compression-based Hawkes discovery and citations to Jalaldoust et al. (2022) and Hlaváčková-Schindler et al. (2024). The detailed comparisons with binned-Hawkes estimation and rank-based latent discovery already appear in v2's Appendix A.

P1.justification: Most prose and section order remain. v3 adds short motivation and explanatory passages, expands future work, adds acknowledgments, and regularizes Appendix A subsection numbering. Numerous cross-references become 'Theorem' even when the displayed item remains a definition, proposition, or lemma.

P2.justification: The document switches throughout to ICLR typography, running headers, and rules, with extensive redistribution of figures, algorithms, and tables. Figure 5 changes from a text-wrapped side figure to a separate centered display, and two appendix tables are added. The ten existing figure graphics themselves are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The new robustness tests and standard deviations add useful empirical evidence. However, Appendix K introduces an incorrect equality reducing a sum of products of exponential bin integrals to twice one bin integral. Q.1–Q.2 also change simulation and graph-matching rules without explaining their relationship to the unchanged retained scores. These benefits and reliability concerns prevent a confident net quality judgment.
